attacks.claim: No authn or authz is described for the cloud Home/Away and schedule APIs that accept device and app writes.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: authn/authz for Home/Away and v1/v2 schedule endpoints

attacks.claim: Not incrementing the anti-rollback counter keeps 4.7 installable, but nothing shows that 4.7 is free of the known vulnerabilities the counter exists to block.
attacks.evidence: 'does not increment the secure-boot anti-rollback counter... so 4.7 remains installable'; ABSENT: 4.7 vulnerability check

attacks.claim: The 'not exposed' claim may not hold in practice. Away Assist sets the thermostat's mode to Away, and existing mode or setpoint fields may already reach partner integrations, which would reveal occupancy indirectly. No test covers this.
attacks.evidence: 'Home/Away state is not exposed through the partner integrations API'; ABSENT: check of whether thermostat mode or setpoint is exposed to partners

attacks.claim: Occupancy inference is new sensitive personal data with 7-day cloud retention. The artifact gives no privacy impact assessment, internal access-control statement, or linkability analysis.
attacks.evidence: 'it is kept 7 days and then deleted'; ABSENT: PIA, internal access restrictions, account linkage

attacks.claim: Away state and schedule sync depend on a single cloud service and an existing CDN contract, and no exit or portability path for stored history is described.
attacks.evidence: 'via existing CDN contract'; ABSENT: exit path for cloud-held Home/Away and schedule data

attacks.claim: Stage 4 has no duration or pacing. A 100% push of about 1.5 TB into the local install windows has no concurrency or bandwidth cap stated.
Egress excludes retries, resumes, and the revert push (another ~1.5 TB). 'Within the monthly commit' gives no headroom figure, and the +0.4% telemetry projection has no baseline or event size.
attacks.evidence: 'within the monthly commit'; 'projected +0.4% on telemetry ingest'

attacks.claim: HIL bench excludes C-wire power-stealing installs, the configuration most prone to brownout and relay chatter, while 4.8 changes reconnect and motion-sensing behaviour that may alter power draw. No power-draw measurement is given.
attacks.evidence: 'no C-wire power stealing' in HIL row; ABSENT: power-stealing test or power-draw measurement

attacks.claim: The 'never interrupted' promise is contradicted by the relay-off install window and by boot-failure loops. A hang that never reaches the post-boot self-test is not clearly covered by the 3-failure revert, and relay state during failed boots is unspecified.
attacks.evidence: 'freeze/heat protection is never interrupted' vs 'relays are held open (off)' and 'fails to boot or fails its post-boot self-test 3 times'

attacks.claim: Alerting omits the signals that matter most. HVAC fault codes and schedule-sync errors appear on the dashboard but do not page, even though HVAC telemetry is a stage gate.
attacks.evidence: 'Pages firmware on-call if boot reverts exceed 0.1%... or offline rate rises 0.5 points'; HVAC fault codes listed only on the dashboard

attacks.claim: The revert path requires 4.8 units to stay reachable over the same OTA path that 4.8 modifies in its reconnect logic. Revert was tested on only 300 qa-fleet units, not on postponed or intermittently offline units.
attacks.evidence: 'push 4.7 to updated units through the same OTA path'; 'Tested on 300 qa-fleet units'

attacks.claim: Revert silently drops schedule periods 5-8 and deletes Away history, with no user-facing notice or restoration path.
attacks.evidence: 'schedules fall back to their v1 copy and Away Assist turns off (Home/Away history is deleted)'

attacks.claim: The cloud v2 discard is specified only for 4.7 edits. Edits from app 9.2 or 9.3 on a unit whose stale v2 copy still exists are unspecified, so a re-upgrade can silently restore the old 8-period schedule over a newer edit.
attacks.evidence: 'When a unit on 4.7 edits its schedule, the cloud discards the stale v2 copy'; ABSENT: handling of v1 edits from other app versions while v2 exists

attacks.claim: Motion sensors often fail to register stationary occupants, so Away mode could engage during night-time 'home' periods. The artifact does not address this, and QA only checks on and off transitions.
attacks.evidence: 'sets Away mode after 2 h with no motion during scheduled home periods'; ABSENT: evidence that stationary or sleeping occupants are detected, or a sleep-period exclusion

attacks.claim: The QA claim that all tests used the production-signed image conflicts with failed-boot injection, which requires a modified or faulted image. The artifact does not show how the failure was induced, so the revert test may not exercise the real path.
attacks.evidence: 'All tests used the production-signed 4.8 image'; 'Failed-boot injection → auto revert to 4.7 | Pass'

attacks.claim: The energy claim is a median from one field trial, but the artifact describes no control group, trial firmware version, or confounder handling. The legal substantiation reference is linked but not summarised.
attacks.evidence: 'cut heating runtime by a median of 6%'; ABSENT: control design, trial firmware version, confounder handling

attacks.claim: Release notes promise two weeks, but the stages total 11 days and stage 4 is open-ended. Gate baselines are undefined, and stage 1 (about 6,100 units) has little power to detect a 0.05% revert rate.
attacks.evidence: 'Rolling out over the next two weeks'; 'HVAC fault telemetry not above 4.7 baseline'; ABSENT: baseline definition

attacks.claim: The employee beta is self-selected and not representative of field installations, so its crash-free figure is weak evidence.
attacks.evidence: 'Employee beta: 1,140 homes for 3 weeks | Crash-free 99.97%'

attacks.claim: The energy claim and the updated privacy notice section 3 appear only in English in the artifact. Canadian consumer claims and Quebec privacy notices need French versions, and none is shown for either.
attacks.evidence: 'Release notes (English and French)' covers release notes only; energy claim quoted in English only; ABSENT: French privacy notice section 3 and French claim text

attacks.claim: 'Some schedule changes were simplified' does not say which periods changed, which makes it hard for users to recover their schedule. Device-side French strings are also not shown.
attacks.evidence: 'Some schedule changes were simplified'; ABSENT: device-side French strings

attacks.claim: A user who edits on 4.7 and later re-upgrades silently loses periods 5-8, and no notice is specified for that path. The simplification message only covers the case where v2 is kept.
attacks.evidence: 'a later re-upgrade starts from the current v1 schedule'; notice shown only 'if v2 had more than 4 periods'

attacks.claim: Accessibility QA covers the app screens. The on-device Away Assist settings screen that the artifact describes is not shown as tested.
attacks.evidence: 'Settings > Away Assist shows what it does and what is stored'; ABSENT: device-side accessibility test

attacks.claim: Dual v1/v2 writes plus cloud discard rules create hidden coupling across firmware, app and cloud, and the test matrix (app versions times firmware versions times revision) is not described.
attacks.evidence: 'It also writes a v1 schedule (4 periods) on every edit'; ABSENT: version-matrix test plan

attacks.claim: No gate-worthy finding. Postpone and deferral behaviour is stated, though a 14-day postpone plus stage timing may leave units on mixed versions for a long time.
attacks.evidence: 'Users can postpone an update up to 14 days from the app.'

attacks.claim: No gate-worthy finding beyond the attacks above.
attacks.evidence: n/a

attacks.claim: The install holds HVAC relays open, and the revert trigger is three failed boots or self-tests, but no maximum time is given for how long relays stay off across that cycle. This can conflict with the stated guarantee that freeze/heat protection is never interrupted, especially in a 02:00-05:00 window on a cold night.
attacks.evidence: "During the ~90 s install, relays are held open (off)." / "If 4.8 fails to boot or fails its post-boot self-test 3 times, the unit reverts to 4.7 automatically." ABSENT: total worst-case relay-off duration across retries and revert, and whether a relay-off boot loop is bounded by the 7 °C deferral.

attacks.claim: The retention promise for Home/Away state conflicts with the cost section, which routes that state into telemetry ingest. The artifact does not state the retention or access controls of the telemetry pipeline, so the 7-day deletion claim is unverified for the copy that actually gets stored.
attacks.evidence: "it is kept 7 days and then deleted" vs "Home/Away state adds ~1 small event per state change; projected +0.4% on telemetry ingest." ABSENT: telemetry retention period, backup retention, and whether Home/Away events are excluded from telemetry.

attacks.claim: The revert path depends on pushing 4.7 over the same OTA path. Auto-revert covers only boot and self-test failures, so a 4.8 bug that leaves the unit online but broken, or that breaks connectivity, may leave units that cannot be reverted. The revert was tested on only 300 qa-fleet units against a 612k fleet.
attacks.evidence: "Revert: push 4.7 to updated units through the same OTA path" / "Tested on 300 `qa-fleet` units." ABSENT: out-of-band recovery for units that lose connectivity on 4.8, and a fallback if the OTA service is the failing component.

attacks.claim: Away Assist treats prolonged stillness as absence, so occupants who are home but sedentary (reading, sleeping on a sofa, medically immobile) get Away setpoints. The QA only checks the timer, not false negatives from stationary occupants or sensor blind spots.
attacks.evidence: "sets Away mode after 2 h with no motion during scheduled 'home' periods" / "Away Assist: off after upgrade by default; on → Away after 2 h no motion" ABSENT: stationary-occupant test, a safety or freeze floor for occupied homes, and an override for vulnerable occupants.

attacks.claim: Schedule data is silently lost on the re-upgrade path. A 4.7 edit discards the v2 copy, so after a later re-upgrade the user's 5-8 period schedule is replaced by the simplified v1 schedule. The only notice is the downgrade-time message, which the user may have dismissed or never seen.
attacks.evidence: "When a unit on 4.7 edits its schedule, the cloud discards the stale v2 copy, so a later re-upgrade starts from the current v1 schedule." ABSENT: user notification on re-upgrade or confirmation before the v2 copy is discarded.

attacks.claim: The energy claim is a published, load-bearing marketing figure, but the artifact does not say that the 2025-26 trial ran the shipping Away Assist algorithm, nor what the spread or significance of the 6% median is. Publishing a point estimate from 412 homes without these is a substantiation risk.
attacks.evidence: "In our 2025-26 field trial of 412 homes, Away Assist cut heating runtime by a median of 6%." ABSENT: whether trial firmware matched 4.8, confidence interval or spread, and whether the trial had a control group.

attacks.claim: Stage-advance criteria for HVAC faults rely on telemetry with no paging threshold, and stage 1 is a 3-day sample of about 6,100 units. Rare HVAC fault codes will likely not reach statistical power at that size, so the gate can pass on silence.
attacks.evidence: "HVAC fault telemetry not above 4.7 baseline" vs "Pages firmware on-call if boot reverts exceed 0.1%... or offline rate rises 0.5 points" (no HVAC paging rule). ABSENT: HVAC fault paging threshold and minimum sample size for the advance decision.

attacks.claim: The HIL matrix does not clearly show whether C-wire-less, power-stealing installs were tested. Those installs are the most likely to brown out when relays are held open for 90 s, and that failure would not appear as a boot revert.
attacks.evidence: "HIL bench: conventional 1H/1C, 2-stage, heat pump + aux, no C-wire power stealing; rev B/C/D | Pass, 0 relay faults over 72 h" ABSENT: explicit power-stealing install test and brownout or reboot result during the install relay-off window.

attacks.claim: The claim that Home/Away state is not exposed through the partner integrations API is asserted without any test or config reference. Occupancy timelines are sensitive, so this claim should be verified before it appears in a privacy notice.
attacks.evidence: "Home/Away state is not exposed through the partner integrations API." ABSENT: test or config evidence for this exclusion.

attacks.claim: Occupancy inference used for Canadian users may trigger Quebec Law 25 obligations around profiling assessment, which the artifact does not address beyond a general legal review reference.
attacks.evidence: "Privacy notice section 3 updated (legal review LGL-4471)." ABSENT: Quebec privacy impact assessment or profiling-specific review.

attacks.claim: The egress budget covers one 2.4 MB pass per unit, but excludes retries from deferred installs, failed installs, and the rollback push of another 1.5 TB if the revert is triggered.
attacks.evidence: "OTA egress: 2.4 MB image × 612k units ≈ 1.5 TB via existing CDN contract, within the monthly commit." ABSENT: retry and rollback egress estimate.

attacks.claim: Postponement is capped at 14 days, but the artifact does not say what happens after that window expires. This may force an install during the install window or during an occupied period.
attacks.evidence: "Users can postpone an update up to 14 days from the app." ABSENT: behavior after the 14-day postponement expires.

attacks.claim: No blocking finding. Image signing and boot-slot design are described, but the authorization model for who can halt the campaign or push a downgrade to 4.7 is not stated.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: authz for 'pause the OTA campaign (one switch)' and for the 4.7 push in Revert.

attacks.claim: Home/Away is an occupancy inference, but the artifact limits retention only for the primary cloud state. Telemetry, logs, and backups are not covered, and telemetry ingest is expected to grow.
attacks.evidence: 'it is kept 7 days and then deleted' / 'Home/Away state adds ~1 small event per state change; projected +0.4% on telemetry ingest.' ABSENT: retention for those telemetry events and backups.

attacks.claim: Load-bearing privacy claims have no test evidence in the QA table: that no raw motion leaves the device, and that Home/Away is absent from partner APIs.
attacks.evidence: 'No raw motion data leaves the thermostat.' / 'Home/Away state is not exposed through the partner integrations API.' ABSENT: network capture or API-exposure test in QA summary.

attacks.claim: No blocking finding. Single CDN contract and vendor-run OTA service are noted, but exit path for OTA delivery is not discussed.
attacks.evidence: 'delivered through the production OTA service' / 'via existing CDN contract'

attacks.claim: Stage 4 jumps to 100% with no pacing, and 612k installs are gated only by a 02:00-05:00 local window. Peak CDN and OTA burst behaviour is not analysed.
Egress is asserted to fit the monthly commit, but no commit size, current usage, or headroom is given, and retries or failed-download re-egress are not budgeted.
attacks.evidence: 'within the monthly commit' — ABSENT: commit size, headroom, retry allowance.

attacks.claim: Paging does not cover HVAC fault codes or self-test failures, even though HVAC fault telemetry is an advance criterion for every rollout stage.
attacks.evidence: 'Pages firmware on-call if boot reverts exceed 0.1% ... or offline rate rises 0.5 points over baseline.' vs 'HVAC fault telemetry not above 4.7 baseline'

attacks.claim: Power loss during the ~90 s install with relays open, and persistence of the 3-failure revert counter across power cycles, are not tested. The QA table covers only failed-boot injection.
attacks.evidence: 'During the ~90 s install, relays are held open (off).' / 'fails its post-boot self-test 3 times' — ABSENT: power-cut-during-install and counter-persistence tests.

attacks.claim: Stage advance gates lack a statistical rule. At about 6,100 units, 'boot-revert rate < 0.05%' allows fewer than 3 events, and 'not above baseline' has no tolerance or sample-size definition.
attacks.evidence: 'boot-revert rate < 0.05%, HVAC fault telemetry not above 4.7 baseline, support contacts per 1k units not above baseline'

attacks.claim: Rollback depends entirely on the OTA channel. A 4.8 unit that is online-but-broken, or offline after the Wi-Fi reconnect change, cannot be reverted, which conflicts with the agreed rule that devices must always be able to return to the previous firmware. No local revert path is described.
attacks.evidence: 'Revert: push 4.7 to updated units through the same OTA path' vs 'Wi-Fi reconnect after router reboot now < 60 s' and 'devices must always be able to return' (agreed rule). ABSENT: local or non-OTA revert.

attacks.claim: Revert and auto-revert silently turn off Away Assist and delete Home/Away history. The auto-revert path has no stated user notice or setting preservation.
attacks.evidence: 'Away Assist turns off (Home/Away history is deleted)' — ABSENT: notice for automatic revert.

attacks.claim: Schedule consistency is specified only for 4.7 edits. App 9.2 or older edits on 4.8 units, and concurrent edits from multiple apps, are not defined. A stale v2 copy could override or conflict with a user's edit.
attacks.evidence: 'When a unit on 4.7 edits its schedule, the cloud discards the stale v2 copy' — ABSENT: rule for 9.2-app edits to a 4.8 unit's v2 schedule.

attacks.claim: Presence is inferred from one wall-mounted sensor, so occupants in other rooms or stationary occupants will trigger false Away. The artifact has no coverage or false-negative test.
attacks.evidence: 'the thermostat's built-in motion sensor sets Away mode after 2 h with no motion during scheduled "home" periods' — ABSENT: multi-room coverage or stationary-occupant test.

attacks.claim: Downgrade and auto-revert drop schedule periods without device-side notice. The 'simplified' message only appears in the app, so comfort and runtime change silently.
attacks.evidence: 'keeping the 4 periods closest to the user's wake / leave / return / sleep anchors' / 'The app shows "Some schedule changes were simplified"'

attacks.claim: The rollback plan depends on app 9.3 working with 4.7 units, but no QA row tests app 9.3 against 4.7 or downgraded units. The claim is unsupported.
attacks.evidence: 'App 9.3 works with both 4.7 and 4.8 units; no app rollback needed.' — QA table lists app 9.3 tests only, with no 4.7-unit row.

attacks.claim: The 'never interrupted' heat-protection claim is contradicted by the artifact's own description of relays being held open during install.
attacks.evidence: 'so freeze/heat protection is never interrupted' vs 'relays are held open (off)' during the ~90 s install.

attacks.claim: Only the low-temperature deferral branch is tested. The >32 °C deferral branch has no evidence.
attacks.evidence: 'Temperature deferral at 5 °C chamber test' — ABSENT: test at >32 °C.

attacks.claim: The employee beta is not representative of the 612k-unit fleet. Three weeks and 1,140 homes cannot support 'no increase in support contacts' at fleet scale.
attacks.evidence: 'Employee beta: 1,140 homes for 3 weeks'

attacks.claim: Release copy says rollout takes two weeks, but the plan is about 11 days plus postponements of up to 14 days, so the copy can be wrong for some users.
attacks.evidence: 'Rolling out over the next two weeks.' vs '3 days' + '4 days' + '4 days' and 'postpone an update up to 14 days'

attacks.claim: No blocking finding. Away Assist is opt-in and off by default, so the value question is limited to the energy claim, which is handled under compliance and evidence.
attacks.evidence: 'Away Assist is off for every user until they turn it on.'

attacks.claim: The install waits for no active HVAC call within a 3-hour overnight window, with no maximum deferral. In winter the install may never run.
attacks.evidence: 'the unit waits until no HVAC call is active' within 'Install window 02:00-05:00 local' — ABSENT: fallback or maximum wait.

attacks.claim: Away Assist can set Away for sedentary, sleeping, or less mobile occupants after 2 h without motion. This drops heating for people who are home but do not move much, and no accessibility consideration is given.
attacks.evidence: 'sets Away mode after 2 h with no motion during scheduled "home" periods' — ABSENT: handling of stationary or sleeping occupants.

attacks.claim: Screen-reader and text-scaling tests cover app 9.3 only. Device-side Settings strings, contrast, and French device text are not tested.
attacks.evidence: 'App 9.3 schedule editor and Away Assist screens with VoiceOver, TalkBack, 200% text' — ABSENT: on-device display and French device strings.

attacks.claim: The energy claim is causal ('cut heating runtime') but the artifact gives no control-group or method description. Published at stage 1 with no evidence summary in the artifact, it risks misleading-advertising exposure in US and Canada.
attacks.evidence: 'In our 2025-26 field trial of 412 homes, Away Assist cut heating runtime by a median of 6%.' — ABSENT: control design in artifact.

attacks.claim: Presence inference is being deployed in Canada, and a Quebec-style privacy impact assessment may be required. The artifact cites only a privacy-notice legal review.
attacks.evidence: 'Privacy notice section 3 updated (legal review LGL-4471).' — ABSENT: privacy impact assessment for the Canadian rollout.

attacks.claim: The release bundles schedule format, Away Assist, humidity sensing, and Wi-Fi changes. Attribution of any boot, HVAC, or offline regression to a single change will be hard.
attacks.evidence: 'What ships' lists four independent changes in one OTA image.

attacks.claim: No additional gate-worthy issue beyond the lenses above.
attacks.evidence: Reviewed the full artifact; no further attack.
